title: No-argument constructors and why they matter
answer: A no-argument constructor takes no parameters. It can provide default initialization and is also required by some frameworks or object-mapping mechanisms that instantiate a type reflectively. AeroTopo's JPA entity `SurveyProject` has a protected no-arg constructor specifically so the persistence framework can instantiate the entity, while application code normally uses the public constructor that supplies required domain values.
